answer_1.quote: We propose a novel approach to biomedical document summarisation whereby we enhance neural models with external domain-specific knowledge in the form of the abstracts of cited papers... The goal is to generate a summary Y = {y1, y2, ..., yt} by modeling the conditional probability distribution P(Y|X∈di, X∈Dc).
answer_1.outputs: Generated abstractive summaries (abstracts) of biomedical papers

answer_2.quote: We report the unigram and bigram overlaps (ROUGE-1 and ROUGE-2, respectively) ... we also include BERTScore (BeS) and BartScore (BaS) to assess the quality of the generated outputs. ... we introduce some readability metrics, e.g. Flesch‑Kincaid (FLK) and Coleman‑Liau Index (CLI), to evaluate the readability of the generated text.

answer_4.quote: We invite 3 qualified evaluators by snowball sampling to rate 30 randomly sampled instances from the testset... the evaluators were provided with the same annotation guide... The four aspects evaluated in the human evaluation were: fluency, readability, relevance, and informativeness.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluators used an annotation guide and rated summaries on a Likert scale (1‑5) for each criterion.
